newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus belt stays dry, new growth slowed.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus belt stays dry, new growth slowed.

text.p: Virtually all areas of the Florida citrus were dry for most of the week week ended November 3, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said, with new growth slowing due to the absence of regular rain.
There were some scattered showers noted on Saturday, but most caretakers on the high sand ridge counties are running their irrigation equipment, FASS said.
New crop early fruit is making good progress, although Fass said it is a little behind the same period last year.
Caretakers are cutting cover crops prior to harvesting and few sprays are still being applied, FASS said.
Additionally, FASS estimated 211,000 boxes of navel oranges harvested in the week ended November 3, up from 183,000 boxes in the previous week and 132,000 boxes in the week ended October 20.
An estimated 547,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended November 3, up from 264,000 boxes the prior week and 171,000 boxes the week ended October 20, FASS said.
